items.title: Weave Router 2.0
items.name: Weave Router 2.0
items.description: Use Claude models in Codex and GPT models in Claude Code on your existing plans, routed to whichever has quota left. Weave Router 2.0 routes each coding agent request to the cheapest model that can get it right. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 and SWE-Atlas it matches GPT-6 Astra at half the cost, 2x faster. Powered by a new classifier that scores task complexity and cache-aware switching that only moves when savings beat the rebuild cost.
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt, I'm Adam, Co-founder of Weave!

The Problem

Coding agents send every request to one model. A one-line config change and a cross-service migration both go to the same frontier model at the same price. Teams are paying frontier rates for routine work, and the bill grows with every agent they add.

Most tools in this space follow one of two flawed approaches:

  • ❌ Gateways – They give you one endpoint and a menu of models. You still pick the model yourself, so nothing actually gets cheaper.

  • ❌ Manual model switching – Flipping /model mid-session breaks your prompt cache, and on long sessions the re-billed context eats the savings.

After running into this on our own agent traffic, we built Weave Router to solve it.

How Weave Router 2.0 is Different 🚀

Weave Router plugs into Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor as a drop-in endpoint. It reads every request your agent makes, scores how hard it is, and sends it to the cheapest model that will get it right.

The benchmarks

We ran 2.0 head to head against GPT-6 Astra, each task run twice (pass@2).

📊 Terminal-Bench 4.0 – Tied pass rate within the confidence interval. 52% of Astra's cost. 2.2x faster.

📊 SWE-Atlas Codebase QnA – Tied pass rate within the confidence interval. 46% of Astra's cost. 2.5x faster.

Full results at weaveos.com/router.

  • 🔹 Complexity-scored routing – A new classifier trained on 10x more real agentic coding sessions routes on task difficulty, not task type. DeepSeek, GLM, and Kimi handle the simple turns. Astra and Fable handle the hard ones.

  • 🔹 Cache-aware switching – 2.0 tracks cache state per provider and per session. It only switches models when the expected savings beat the cost of rebuilding the cache. This is where most of the cost win comes from.

  • 🔹 Multi-subscription routing – Use Claude models inside Codex and GPT models inside Claude Code. Route by complexity, by cost, or by whichever plan still has quota this month.

Who is this for?

If you or your team run coding agents daily, Weave Router gets you Astra-level results at about half the cost and more than twice the speed, without changing your tools.

🔗 Get started today

Try it at weaveos.com/router. Install with one command: npx @workweave/router. Source-available under Elastic License 2.0. Teams of 50+ engineers can book time with our FDEs.

items.summary: AI-native customer support and feedback agent
items.description: Most teams run a helpdesk, a feedback board and a survey tool, then copy between them all week. ProductBridge is one system. An AI agent answers support chats from your help center, calls your APIs via tools, workflows and MCP, and hands off when it should. Every chat, survey and vote is captured, deduplicated and scored by reach and revenue, so your roadmap runs on evidence, not opinions. Ship it and everyone who asked is notified. MCP for Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. Flat pricing, free plan.
top_comments: Hey Product Hunt 👋 Hareesh here, founder of ProductBridge. In March we launched here as an AI agent that collects feedback from Slack, Intercom, review sites and your feedback board, merges the duplicates, and turns the pile into a roadmap. You sent it to #1 for the day. Thank you for that 🙏 We spent the six months since watching how teams actually used it, and one pattern kept showing up: the feature request almost never started on the feedback board. It started as a support conversation, in a different tool, attached to a different customer record. Support saw it first, product saw it last, and nobody told the customer when it shipped. So we built the other half. ProductBridge is now AI-native customer support and feedback on one customer record: 💬 Live chat + shared inbox — chat and email together, with assignments, SLAs and CSAT 🤖 AI support agent — grounded on your help center, calls your APIs through tools and workflows, and hands off to a human when it should 📚 Help center — write an article once and the agent answers from it 📊 Surveys — NPS, CSAT and CES inside your product, with responses flowing into the same feedback intelligence 🔌 MCP server — 36 tools, so you can ask Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor what your customers are asking for 🔁 The same closed loop as before — a support chat becomes a feature request, gets scored by reach and revenue, and the customer who asked is notified when it ships What hasn't changed: flat price. No per-seat, no per-tracked-user, no per-resolution fees. There's a free plan, most teams are live in about 15 minutes, and if you're on Canny, Featurebase or Intercom we'll help you move. One question for you 👇 What's the one thing your support + feedback stack still makes you copy-paste by hand? That's usually where we find the next thing to build. I'll be here all day answering questions 🚀
All the best

items.title: ProductBridge
items.name: ProductBridge
items.summary: AI-native customer support and feedback agent
items.description: Most teams run a helpdesk, a feedback board and a survey tool, then copy between them all week. ProductBridge is one system. An AI agent answers support chats from your help center, calls your APIs via tools, workflows and MCP, and hands off when it should. Every chat, survey and vote is captured, deduplicated and scored by reach and revenue, so your roadmap runs on evidence, not opinions. Ship it and everyone who asked is notified. MCP for Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. Flat pricing, free plan.
top_comments: Hey Product Hunt 👋 Hareesh here, founder of ProductBridge. In March we launched here as an AI agent that collects feedback from Slack, Intercom, review sites and your feedback board, merges the duplicates, and turns the pile into a roadmap. You sent it to #1 for the day. Thank you for that 🙏 We spent the six months since watching how teams actually used it, and one pattern kept showing up: the feature request almost never started on the feedback board. It started as a support conversation, in a different tool, attached to a different customer record. Support saw it first, product saw it last, and nobody told the customer when it shipped. So we built the other half. ProductBridge is now AI-native customer support and feedback on one customer record: 💬 Live chat + shared inbox — chat and email together, with assignments, SLAs and CSAT 🤖 AI support agent — grounded on your help center, calls your APIs through tools and workflows, and hands off to a human when it should 📚 Help center — write an article once and the agent answers from it 📊 Surveys — NPS, CSAT and CES inside your product, with responses flowing into the same feedback intelligence 🔌 MCP server — 36 tools, so you can ask Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor what your customers are asking for 🔁 The same closed loop as before — a support chat becomes a feature request, gets scored by reach and revenue, and the customer who asked is notified when it ships What hasn't changed: flat price. No per-seat, no per-tracked-user, no per-resolution fees. There's a free plan, most teams are live in about 15 minutes, and if you're on Canny, Featurebase or Intercom we'll help you move. One question for you 👇 What's the one thing your support + feedback stack still makes you copy-paste by hand? That's usually where we find the next thing to build. I'll be here all day answering questions 🚀
All the best
